conventions.unit: metres, FBX unit scale 1 (file units cm, Unity useFileScale on)
conventions.origin: feet on y = 0, centred on x and z
conventions.rig: Humanoid, Mixamo bone names without prefix (Hips, Spine, Spine1, Spine2, Neck, Head, Left/RightShoulder, Arm, ForeArm, Hand, UpLeg, Leg, Foot, ToeBase). 22 mapped bones for the Meshy-style rigs (no fingers), 52 for the Enforcer (fingers). Avatar: Create From This Model, set in each .fbx.meta; Unity maps it unaided (checked: valid, human).
conventions.lods: one FBX per figure holds the skeleton and every LOD as a skinned mesh named <id>_LOD0.. ; Unity builds the LODGroup from the names. Skin weights: 4 per vertex.
conventions.materials: URP Lit .mat per texture set, bound by name in the .fbx.meta. Matte, as the world is (Glint, briefs/020/figures-render.md): the maps are albedo (sRGB) and normal for the 1024 and 2048 sets, plus on the cell and cast a metallic map (R metallic 0..0.6 only on real trim, G occlusion, A smoothness 0.15..0.28 on cloth, skin and hair and up to 0.55 on trim; the map is 1024 px even under a 2048 material). The 512 LOD (what play zoom draws) and every crowd material have no metallic map: _Metallic 0, _Smoothness 0.15. The Tech visor is _Smoothness 0.75 with an emission map; his albedo blacks are lifted (a black outfit keeps its shape in shade).
conventions.clips: People/Clips/<name>.fbx: Mixamo library files copied as they are (clip only, 30 fps, in place), each with a Humanoid .meta and one clip named <name>. Any Humanoid figure plays any clip. loop flags are set in the meta; root motion is not baked into the pose, so leave Apply Root Motion off and move the object from the sim.
conventions.tintedVariants: security, driver, councillor, rival and fixer are recolours of another model: only the albedo changed (hue window, skin and hair outside it).

playRoles.body/<key>: the same figure as the person, playing `lying` (or laid flat as the capsule is); `carried` over the carrier's shoulder

missing: Fixer: a real model now (Sky, 2026-10-18): Tripo 3.1 from a Seedream front A-pose sheet of the Fixer cropped from the latest cell lineup (ivory and black), hem shortened to above the knee, no briefcase. $0.7 spent (store characters/fixer_P4-6/spend.json). The briefcase is not modelled: it is a prop for the right Hand bone. The pencil-cut dress hugs both thighs, so it stretches across the legs in a long stride (the hem faces at about 0.64 m; fine at play zoom, visible in the follow view): if it reads badly, a slit or a looser hem is a one-line edit to the sheet prompt (`tools/figures/fixer_gen.py`) and a $0.6 regeneration.

Enforcer: G3 (the style pick) is an unrigged Tripo mesh (characters/enforcer_G3/02_mesh/tripo_p1/model.glb). G2, rigged, is the stand-in: grey-bearded man, cream knee-length coat over a black suit with gold trim. Both coats are below the hip, against the no-long-coat rule: they held in the stretch test (no torn faces in a walk-and-bend pose) but should go when G3 is rigged.
Tech: the older outfit (sleeveless vest, cargo skirt-shorts to the knee, sandals, cyan visor and bands), not the 16 Oct final. Visor and trim are an emission map.

Councillor Vale: no design and no model. Stand-in is commuter D4 (blond, silver bomber, navy jumpsuit turned deep teal), at 8k. The official driver is commuter D2 (chrome visor helmet, coral uniform turned mint), at 8k.

Props: none. The models hold nothing. The aim, shoot and draw clips pose the arms for a rifle or pistol; weapons, the briefcase, a phone are Latch's attachments on the Hand bones (Humanoid RightHand / LeftHand).
Hands: the Meshy-style rigs (everyone but the Enforcer) have no finger bones; hands are mitten shapes. Fine at 53 px, visible only in the follow view.

Carrying Vale: Mixamo has `carry` (the carrier holds a load in front, standing) and `carried` (the limp body) but no walking-while-carrying. First pass: carrier plays walk, body plays carried at the shoulder (the capsule lift of 1.15 m). A load layer on walk would be Latch's.
Knockout and kill clips are one-sided and not synced (knockout 5.6 s, kill 4.4 to 5 s). Time the body falling to the sim's event; each ends lying, so the body can switch to `lying` after.

Left out on purpose: commuter D3 (shin-length trench coat), commuter D5 (long cape), worker D2 (calf-length cape; the cloth was a separate simulated sheet in the VAT crowd), shopper D5 (a child in a bubble helmet). All in the store if wanted.
Elders: one (EL1, a woman). No male elder, no child, no figure in a wheeled or seated pose. Seated café patrons are not covered (exteriors: customers come and go).
Crowd variety is nine looks plus the three café staff; recolours (hue windows in tools/figures/figures.json) would add more cheaply.

Not measured here: GPU time. Triangle counts at play zoom are the last LOD of each figure (1.5k cell and cast, about 1.5k crowd): 100 figures on screen is about 150k triangles and 100 skinned renderers, so the cost to watch is skinning and animator updates, not triangles. Redline's 4.5 ms is for Latch to measure on the Air with the real scene.
The contact sheets are from a scratch Unity project (built-in Standard shader, one sun, no grade, no shadows). The look in the game's URP scene with Glint's grade will differ.

Against the latest cell lineup (cell-lineup-latest.png, Sky 2026-10-18): Scout S1-2 is near (same ivory hooded jacket, black harness, shorts, fingerless gloves and sneakers; the lineup adds the black backpack and chrome-banded shorts, and ours has brass trim). Tech F2-1 is far (the lineup is a sleeveless black wrap top with an ivory sash, wide black-and-ivory pleated hakama trousers with cyan piping, chrome bracers, goggles pushed up, black sneakers; ours is a black vest, cargo skirt-shorts to the knee, sandals, a cyan visor over the eyes and cyan bands: only the dreadlocks, the black and the cyan carry over). Enforcer G2 is half way (same grey-bearded man in sunglasses with a knee-length coat and white boots; the lineup is mostly black with ivory panels and chrome bands and a big chrome rifle, ours is cream with a black suit and gold trim, no rifle).
forLatch: 1. Get the files: `bun tools/figures/run.ts` builds out/people-models/People (needs Blender and the store); `--install` mirrors it to unity/Assets/Suborned/People. Git-ignore that folder like Kit/ (97 MB). Splice may want a hash-checked copy step like the kit's.

2. Everything is imported by its .meta: figures as Humanoid with an avatar from the model, textures with the right colour space, materials bound by name (URP Lit), clips Humanoid with loops set. Checked in Unity 6000.6.2f1 with URP 17.6: avatars valid, LOD groups made, materials resolve.

3. Per figure build a prefab: the FBX root (LODGroup from the names; set the transition heights from `lodScreenHeights`), an Animator with the FBX's avatar and one shared AnimatorController, a CapsuleCollider (1.75 m, radius 0.4) for clicks (the models carry none), Apply Root Motion off. The figure faces +Z; turn the object to the heading the capsule faces.

5. Mapping from the play scene: `playRoles`, `families` and `jobBlocks` in the manifest. Pick from a pool by the person's id so the same person always looks the same. Keys with no entry keep their capsule.

6. The family tints in HostViews (café peach, office teal, guard, driver) are no longer needed: the figures carry their own colours. The signals (cones, rings, price chips, fight tracers) stay as they are.

4. One AnimatorController for all (FigureBuild already makes it). Cross-fade with `CrossFadeInFixedTime(state, 0.15f)`, not `CrossFade(state, 0.15f)`: the second is a fraction of the clip, and an idle of 8.8 s blends for 1.3 s (the Scout's hands stayed on her hips after she stopped). The fourth argument of CrossFade is seconds, not a 0..1 phase.
5. Mapping from the play scene: `playRoles`, `families` and `jobBlocks` in the manifest.

6. Stride: `naturalSpeedMs` per locomotion clip was re-measured in Unity (walk 1.29, walk_f 0.99, run 2.52, walk_armed 2.44, run_armed 3.11 m/s). `walk_armed` and `run_armed` are fast clips: below about 2 m/s play `walk` (or `walk_f`) and keep the weapon in the aim pose, or the armed walk plays at 0.6x in slow motion.

7. Carried and lying: `carried` is now the limp lying clip. Put the figure at the carrier's shoulder with the object's own height at 1.15 m (the clip adds 0.13 m of hips) and turn it 90 degrees to the carrier's heading so it lies across the shoulders; never add the lift twice (the old `carried` clip climbed from the ground to 1.4 m by itself, and the lift made Vale fly). `lying` and the knockout and kill clips end on the ground: place the figure at the body's point (no lift).
8. Standing, walking and running clips now put the soles on the ground themselves (Root Transform Position (Y): Based Upon Feet; the lying, falling and carried clips keep the original height).

9. Materials are matte now (metallic 0, smoothness 0.15 on the no-map materials; the mapped ones rebaked to the world's cloth). If a figure is still too bright, change `_Smoothness` on its material, not the map.

entry.prompt: Character model sheet for 3D modelling of the character in the reference image, who is seen from behind: the same woman with exactly the same outfit, cut, colours, materials and trims, now shown from the FRONT. The outfit: a fitted dress of vertical panels in ivory and black, with fine pinstripe panels, a high halter neckline with bare shoulders, long fitted ivory sleeves worn from the shoulder to the wrist as separate sleeves, the dress hem cut shorter than in the reference to sit a clear hand's width above the kneecap, so the knees show, straight and clean, nothing flowing or trailing below it; a high ponytail of long straight black hair; two-tone ivory and black heeled ankle boots with a chrome heel accent. The briefcase is removed: nothing is held or attached. Full body from head to toe, centred, front view, standing in a strict A-pose: both arms straight and held 45 degrees out from the body, a clear gap of air between each arm and the torso and between each hand and the hips, palms facing the thighs, fingers relaxed; legs straight with the feet shoulder-width apart so the thighs do not touch. Neutral expression. Even soft shadowless studio light, no cast shadows, no floor, plain background. The same rendering style as the reference image, crisp edges. Original design, not resembling any real person or film character. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermark.

clips.name: idle_alt
clips.use: second idle so a crowd does not breathe in step

clips.name: walk_f
clips.use: walk, women (crowd, staff): a tough strut with a full arm swing (Female_Walk swings the arms half as far)

clips.name: run_lean
clips.use: the cell's run (double-click): a leaning sprint, longer stride and flight than run (the old web testbed's run, retargeted); keep run for the crowd and panic

clips.name: panic
clips.use: startled or panicking on the spot

clips.name: cower
clips.use: duck and cover (1.5 s); hold the last frame

clips.name: knockout
clips.use: knocked out: the victim goes down and ends lying (5.6 s)

clips.name: kill_victim
clips.use: killed: falls and ends lying (4.4 s)

clips.name: kill_victim_back
clips.use: killed from the front: falls backward (3.7 s)

clips.name: kill_attacker
clips.use: the Enforcer kills (5 s); pairs with kill_victim by eye, not by sync

clips.name: carried
clips.use: the carried body, limp and flat: the figure is placed at the carrier's shoulder (hips about 0.13 m above the object; no library clip drapes a body over a shoulder: Being_Carried is a pick-up sequence that climbs from the ground to 1.4 m)
